label: End-of-episode D1 (low value, esp. after reward)
explanation: Fires almost only at D1 (98.5% of mass; never at GO, rare at D2) in the last ~10 trials of the episode (ep_trial 90-99 holds 99.9% of mass; zero activity before trial 80). It tracks the model value head falling toward episode end: all activity is in the lowest value bin (<5.2). Within that, a reward input at D1 makes it fire at higher value (value < 4 with in_rew = 1, or value < 3 regardless); 89% of mass is on rewarded D1 steps. Magnitude grows as the episode end approaches (top windows peak at the last trial in the window, rising trial by trial). Phase + ep_trial >= 93 gives F1 0.61; the value-based predicate is better (dev F1 0.82, mass recall 0.98). Uses only observed/internal quantities (value is the model own output; in_rew is the current input).

issues: Factual claims check out on dev: D1 holds 98.5% of the mass, GO has 0 active steps, D2 1.5%. No activity in ep_trial 0-79, 20 active steps in 80-89, 99.9% of the mass in 90-99. 100% of the mass is in the lowest value bin (<5.22). in_rew=1 holds 88.8%. The ep_trial>=93 position predicate scores dev F1 0.608 and the recorded predicate dev F1 0.822; the test numbers match the report (P 0.711, R 0.926, F1 0.804, mass recall 0.972).

Small overstatement: 'peaks at the last trial in the window' is true of the top windows, but overall mass at rel+0 (0.281) and rel+1 (0.275) is about equal. That fits the episode-end ramp and is not a contradiction.

No systematic counterexample class. Precision of the predicate is flat across prev_action (0.70/0.76), good state (0.72/0.74), start_high (0.76/0.69), choice logit and prev_common (0.71 common vs 0.85 rare, a mild skew). Restricting to ep_trial<93 leaves only 1047 predicted steps.

Misses (1.9% of mass on dev, 2.8% on test) are scattered weak D2 activations and sub-threshold D1 steps. False positives are mostly the first predicted D1 steps of the end-of-episode ramp, before the unit has crossed its threshold. That is a cutoff effect, not a missing variable.

The value cutoffs are a bit loose. Tightening them to value<3.8 with reward, or value<2.8 otherwise, raises dev F1 from 0.822 to 0.861 and test F1 from 0.804 to 0.845. The concept is unchanged, so this is a refinement and not a refutation.
